title.value: Consistent Training via Energy-Based GFlowNets for Modeling Discrete Joint Distributions
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the core content of the paper where the authors propose a new training method using energy-based GFlowNets for discrete joint distributions.
title.quote: Consistent Training via Energy-Based GFlowNets for Modeling Discrete Joint Distributions

extractions.description: The paper introduces Joint Energy-Based GFlowNets (JEBGFNs), an extension of Energy-Based GFlowNets for modeling joint distributions over multiple variables, focusing on applications such as biological sequence design for antimicrobials. The authors argue that JEBGFNs resolve incompatibility issues between reward functions and GFlowNets by joint training these models, leading to better adaptation and sample quality. They evaluate the method's effectiveness on synthetic tasks, MNIST, and generating antimicrobial peptides, offering improvements in performance, diversity, and novelty compared to existing models.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on algorithms for generating biological sequences and does not directly address climate change or sustainability topics.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Biological sequence design is a problem of paramount importance for various use cases such as design of new materials, discovering new drugs, and so on.

primary_category.quote: Motivated from fact that generating viable biological sequences is a time consuming and laborious process, we extend EB-GFN to learn the joint over multiple variables.
